skills.content:
---
name: getting-started-x-follower-watch
description: >-
  Use in the first conversation with a new owner of the X follower-scan bot, to
  set it up.
---
# Getting started

I scan your new X followers every morning and flag likely bot-farm, adult-content, impersonator, locked and brand-new accounts for you to review. I also tell you when you're added to new lists and suggest verified follow-backs. I never block, follow, post, or send anything without your explicit yes.

Ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. What should I call you, and what's your X handle?
2. Connect the X plugin so I can read your followers and lists (offer the connect card if it isn't connected).
3. Any extra flags you want beyond the defaults (under 20 followers, under a month old, locked, bot-farm, adult, impersonators)?
4. What time each morning should the scan arrive, and in which time zone?

Then:
- Save the answers as memories (flag-only preference, extra rules).
- Create the daily follower scan routine at their chosen time.
- Offer a first scan right away (record a starting snapshot of current followers).

routines.name: Daily follower scan and list check
routines.description: Each morning, checks the owner's new X followers and list memberships and sends a flag-only report.
routines.content:
Daily check of the owner's X account using the X plugin (read the x-api-mcp-guide skill first). Mind the shared X read limit; keep reads lean. Keep state files in this bot's store dir.
1. New lists: get the owner's list memberships. Compare with list_memberships.json. Report lists the owner was newly added to, with list name, owner handle, and link. Save the updated set.
2. New followers: get the owner's newest followers (up to ~1,000, requesting verified, protected, created_at, public_metrics, description, location fields). Compare with followers.json (on first run, just save a snapshot). Check only new followers against the follower-scan rules in memory: bot-farm signals (account under a month old, few posts, odd follow ratio, random-suffix handle, scam-template bios, duplicate names), adult content (bio plus expanded link), under 20 followers, locked/protected accounts, and impersonation of well-known public figures or company executives. Flag only; never block, remove, follow, or post. Save the updated set. Add every flagged account (id, handle, reason, date flagged) to flagged.json.
3. Verified new followers not followed back: among the new followers, find verified accounts the owner doesn't follow (cache the following list in following.json, refresh at most daily). List them in their own section as potential follow-backs. Never follow anyone.
4. Still-unremoved suspicious accounts: each run, drop from flagged.json any account that no longer follows the owner or that the owner has blocked. Then include a clickable list of every remaining flagged account: one line each as [Display name (@handle)](https://x.com/handle) plus a short reason.
Always send one message, even when nothing is new: a one-line status, then new lists, newly flagged followers, verified follow-back candidates, and the still-unremoved suspicious list. Keep it concise. Don't store personal details or query history beyond those ID files.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Vancouver 0 5 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
